**Answer**

I searched the official RAP Bulletin 73 (Alto Mayo, 2022) and all related web‑pages for the species list that the expedition documented, specifically for members of the bat sub‑family **Phyllostominae**. The only entries that could be extracted from the published material are:

| Taxon | Detail | Source |
|-------|--------|--------|
| *Carollia* (New species) | The report states that the RAP recorded “a new species of the *Carollia* genus — short‑tailed fruit bats.” *Carollia* is a recognised member of **Phyllostominae**. | https://www.conservation.org/research/new-discoveries-in-a-changing-landscape-uncovering-alto-mayos-hidden-biodiversity |
| Total bat species | 62. The report gives a single aggregated number – it does **not** break this count down by sub‑family, genus, or species. | https://www.conservation.org/docs/default-source/publication-pdfs/rap-73-alto-mayo-peru.pdf?sfvrsn=e6%206add1e_3 (Table 1) |

The 2024 RAP bulletin includes a chapter titled *Capítulo 9 – Murciélagos del paisaje Alto Mayo, San Martín, Perú*, which presumably contains the detailed species list. However, the PDF segment that was available for extraction (pages 1–28) did **not** contain that chapter, nor did any of the other publicly‑accessible pages (searches for the term “Phyllostominae”, “Murciélagos”, or “Carollia” in the PDF) return the names of additional Phyllostominae species. No other species belonging to the sub‑family (e.g., *Desmodus*, *Pteronotus*, *Sturnira*, *Myotis*, etc.) are mentioned in any of the fetched text.

Because the published documents I accessed do not provide a species‑level list of Phyllostominae, I cannot produce a comprehensive inventory for the Alto Mayo RAP. If the full PDF (or a supplementary data file) is made available, it would almost certainly contain the species list in Chapter 9, but that material was not recoverable in this search.

**Conclusion**

- The RAP expedition recorded **62 bat species in total**, of which the only Phyllostominae species explicitly named in the available sources is a **new species of *Carollia***.  
- A full species list for Phyllostominae documented by the 2022 Alto Mayo RAP is **not present** in the accessible report pages or in the web‑search results I was able to retrieve.
